question: What if gravity switched off for 5 seconds?
answer_in_one_line: Nothing flies off by itself: whatever sits still stays put (the spinning ground only sinks ten inches away from under a chair in five seconds), but anything that was already moving keeps its speed, so a pancake flipped at eight feet a second never comes back and a one-foot hop carries Gus thirty-two feet up in four seconds, to the height of an Olympic diving tower, from where he comes down at thirty miles an hour.

why_this_one: The trend file offers no fresh row that passes all four tests, so this is the best unused tier A entry of the topic bank from a cluster that neither of the last two episodes used (a plane, then space). Everybody has wondered what would happen if gravity let go for a moment, and everybody expects to float away or be flung off the spinning planet. The title is seven plain words in the 'for 5 seconds' frame that works for small channels. The surprise is that nothing happens to whoever sits still (ten inches in five seconds from the Earth's spin) and that one number carries the rest: a one-foot hop is eight feet a second, and with no brake that is thirty-two feet in four seconds. The mechanism (gravity is a brake on anything going up) is carried by a ball rolled up a hill and across a flat floor. It is drawable with the kit's garden and flat cards. Nobody is hurt: Gus lands in a pool inside his fishbowl helmet and comes up with a pancake on his head; the scenario needs gravity to be switched off, so there is nothing a child could copy.
